subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but this adds compatibility-sensitive config and provider/session routing surface that automation should not finalize without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor additive per-agent overrides
options.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics with defaults, and repair/review the open PR as the implementation path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Support only `agents.list[].compaction.model` for provider/cost isolation and defer broader compaction/contextPruning knobs to a follow-up design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline the config expansion and close or redirect the implementation PRs, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor additive per-agent overrides
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics with defaults, and repair/review the open PR as the implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: The active closing PR is assigned to this handle, making them the best current routing owner for the PR-vs-replacement decision.
